interactions.summary: Asked how the Divine Comedy felt the first time he read it, Jiang narrates months of bewilderment followed by a dreamlike visitation in which Dante told him to think about love, after which the poem began opening up and the universe seemed to answer his will.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student prompt and Jiang autobiographical answer

interactions.summary: A student compares Dante's esotericism to soft rather than hard magic, and Jiang agrees in part before redoubling his claim that the poem is perfect, magical, and effectively God's word spoken through Dante's poetry.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student interpretive proposal and Jiang response

claims.claim: Jiang says that when he first began reading the Divine Comedy about four years earlier, he had no idea what he was reading and remained confused for many months.
claims.temporal_scope: Personal recollection told on 2026-06-18 about an earlier reading period.

claims.claim: Jiang says explanatory videos about the Divine Comedy only made him more confused rather than clarifying the poem.
Jiang says he persisted with Dante because he wanted to teach Great Books to his high-school students even though he felt like he would be a complete idiot.
Jiang says that one morning it felt as though Dante came into his dreams and told him that love was the key to understanding the Divine Comedy.
Jiang says the poem began opening up once he followed the path of love, and he links that breakthrough back to Piccarda's logic that where there is will there is a way.
claims.temporal_scope: Interpretive and autobiographical claim stated on 2026-06-18.

claims.claim: Jiang says that when one truly wants understanding, the universe responds and guides one to the right path, even if not in the expected way.
A student argues that Dante's esotericism resembles soft magic more than hard magic, while later occult ritualism resembles the harder form because actions are expected to produce results.
Jiang says he agrees with the student's soft-magic comparison and then reiterates that the Divine Comedy is the word of God or the universe speaking through Dante.
claims.temporal_scope: Interpretive agreement and theological claim stated on 2026-06-18.

claims.claim: Jiang says he has not been able to find a flaw in the Divine Comedy and praises its structure, language, and economy of ideas as signs of perfection.
Jiang says the more one studies the Divine Comedy the more one discovers, and he contrasts that richness with the Bible, which he calls a complete mess.
Jiang says Dante's poetry feels like God or the universe taking possession of him, which is why the poem can feel perfect to listeners.
Jiang says that after the break he will present the official Catholic history and then show how Dante offers a new understanding of God and Jesus.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang's account of Dante entering his dreams and giving him the key word 'love' becomes the turning point in his own access to the poem.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves the packet's most vivid autobiographical scene and links interpretation to desire, revelation, and vocation rather than technique alone.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang turns the struggle to read Dante into a cosmic rule: when you really want something, the universe responds.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This carries the packet's strongest causal model about will, desire, and guidance.

signature_moments.moment: Dante's poetry is described as God taking possession of the poet and singing through him.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It condenses Jiang's sacral understanding of poetic inspiration and his claim that the poem's perfection is inseparable from divine utterance.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The student's fantasy-fiction analogy for a magical order where effects appear without a fully predictable ritual calculus, which he uses to describe Dante's esotericism and Catholic miracle logic.
The student's contrasting analogy for ritual systems where one performs a known act and expects a determinate result, which he associates with later occult development.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-06-18 Jiang explicitly narrates his own Dante breakthrough as dream-guided and love-centered, then binds that autobiographical testimony to a broader claim that the Divine Comedy is divine speech, magical in operation, and worth lifelong study.
